Cabe: Rarely prone to just sitting around and staring out into space, thinking of nothing, Cabe uses his brain and rarely rushes head-long into things. I suppose many might describe him as being a little serious, but honestly, do you think success comes from just pure luck? Not a chance. You need to work at it, you need to be prepared and you need to be able to think on your feet and to adapt. He'd make quite a good barrister, actually. Whatever he does and however he does it, you can expect Cabe to apply himself.
Cabel: Cabel makes an excellent middleman in business and he can look after himself if he gets lost on a hiking trip in the Rockies, the Amazon or the Flinders Ranges, depending on the scale of his injuries, naturally.
Cable: I wonder if his parents ever shagged on the beach in Broome, Western Australia…..anyway, some advice Cable: If you don’t get outside for work and for life and get active, you’re going to turn into a reasonably non-functioning drug addict. Good luck and peace out.
Cadel: Like a fighter pilot with his thumb hovering over the trigger, Cadel is calm and primed but....does he believe?
Caden:
Listen, Caden, do what you want with your life, become anything you decide, but you don’t have to get a labouring trade just because all your friends have. The world is a massive, amazing place and you’re no fool. There’s also no rush. Take your time. Expand your mind and travel, and see what takes your fancy. For the time being forget about the gym and trying to attain a 6-pack.
Good luck… 
(Note: We’ll offer up Caden’s Name Theory a little later - Management.)
Caelan: A professional sailor on a racing yacht. He'd never tell his skipper but he's never really cared about winning or losing. He's never been that good at school or handling things like money, he just loves sailing fast and being out there. I have no idea what he'll do if he gets injured.
Caelin: Caielin is the name of one of those Sleepy Sharks that comes in close to the shore at night time. He moves through the water easily and with grace and while looking a little menacing, he's actually quite placid. He won’t bite and the only way you'll get hurt is if you try and wrestle him because, in close, his skin is incredibly tough and abrasive.
Caellan: Interesting how some names pour a person into a life of an almost quiet recluse. No, Caellan isn't one of those, but you can't pick him by looking at him. Most of his thoughts he keeps to himself. Why is that? We're not sure. Time - he seems to have a lot of it. Girls too, if we thought about it, but his reticence to smile openly often leaves most people guessing. A message from the commentary box, brother: Don't stay inside. It'll kill you. Get outside and use your body. Amen.
Caiden: Caiden's motives are often unclear. They're not malicious or devious, he's not like that, generally, he just keeps most of his plans to himself because he doesn't usually see why they should effect anyone else. He's quite a capable young man.
Caillan: Who, Caillan? Composed and sedate? I fuckin' doubt it. He's more like in-your-face, wondering what you did with the stash. And you better find it too - he's not one for waiting around.
Cain: Cain is almost identical to Caine, so please check him out, below, but this one is just a teency bit more impatient and uncertain.
Caine: Possessing something like a laissez faire attitude to just about everything, Caine may look like a straggler but don't be fooled. There's alot going on behind the scenes here and he is extremely independent. Good mates with Mark and Fergus.
Cale: Cale is another country boy who grew up swimming in channels and rivers, as well as getting pissed and shat on by the cows in the diary shed at 4 in the morning. His success in the arena of romance is largely achieved by pure luck, but he rides that like everything else and these days he does quite nicely, walking a straight line to those things he covets – utes, beer, new boots.
Caleb: The Commander ends the briefing and studies the faces of the four young pilots in front of him, knowing full-well that even a successful mission would mean at least two of them will probably not make it back. He is already aware that Caleb, the squadron leader, would lay his life down if he had to – especially given the thousands at risk if they fail – but this is what they were trained to do. It’s why he was selected to lead the mission. And, if all hell breaks loose and he can’t make it back to the mainland he’s pretty sure Caleb will be smiling when he meets his maker. “Godspeed gentlemen,” the Commander says. The men rise and prepare to fly into battle...
Calen: Ah huh, yep, we know - he’s a normal sort of guy who, deep down, doesn’t actually really want to do anything.
Caley: People warm to Caley very quickly and he's never a thug. He was (and is) inexpensive and easy to raise and he's active in both body and mind. Some people just feel like they’re easy to deal with and Caley is definitely one of these.
Calix:
Option A:  Another botanist. Enjoys the jungle and any wild-life ecology studies.

Option B:  Graphic designer.
Callais: Callais, did they name you that because you were conceived on French shores, or because you were conceived in a Maccas carpark? Mmmm, we'll ponder that. Anyway, Callais needs to stand up for himself a little more. Don't be afraid to ditch your friends if they're rude and childish dickheads, yeah?
Callan: Callan appears to be perpetually preoccupied, but is he? Either way, we know he’s more sensitive that he looks because he blushes easily, which is evidence he is far more empathetic than we imagined.
Callen:
And here we have yet another young Millennial who, when finally standing and motivated doesn’t move slowly. He’s prompt, he’s physically active and, indeed, you might even describe him as a normal, nice young fellow who sits squarely in the middle of most bell curves. 
Callen, what do you have to say about this?…
Calvin: Slight of build. We’d suggest you beware of his pranks but they’re so well thought out and executed that you can’t prepare for them anyway.
Cam: Cam is a tremendous fellow. Relaxed with an edge, he understands women and men, he knows who he is and, most importantly, as a never-say-die optimist he endeavours to like everything.
Camden: The name of a big fluffy beach towel with a large ego. Pink and yellow.
Cameron:
Cameron, if he’s known by no other nickname, is a deep thinking man – deciding how to put out the garbage on a Monday night sometimes requires an intricate analysis, for instance – but the sad fact of the matter is that Cameron, the word, looks and sounds like something that a youth might extract from his or her nose.  
“Bloody hell!” Clint might say to Billy one afternoon, after they’ve robbed a defenceless grandmother and left her lying in the street. “Check out this Cameron!”
Camo: He was a surf coach in Brazil for a while until he tired of the number of women chasing him. Then he went to Portugal and did the same thing until he ran out of money, and condoms. Anyone heard from him lately?...
Campbell: As a rather formal and boring secondary school college made of old red bricks, all Campbell wants to do is leave some kind of legacy.
Cap:
In a past life, Cap was a wonderful and courageous medic in the trenches during WWI. Despite the obvious dangers, he'd repeatedly run out there into no man's land with bullets whistling all about, his only goal the screams of a young man with half his legs blown off, or some such catastrophic scene. Can you imagine people actually did this?

Anyway, no matter how fast his heart was beating and no matter how scared he himself was, he'd arrive with a smile and a never say die attitude, and he'd do the best he could.  Someone should've given him a posthumous medal for bravery.

In this life, whatever Cap is doing and however he is going about his business, you can be rest assured not much has changed. 

Nice one Cap.
Cappi: Cappi hugs his children and grandchildren to the point of embarrassment. Always laughing, Cappi lets his wife run the affairs of the house, but he definitely understands the benefits of a hard day’s work. He’ll always be the joker.
Carl: The brand new livestock fence. His posts are new and chemically treated, they are exactly perpendicular to the ground and he sports new grade 9 fencing wire. He is tough to get passed in a hurry, however, and often you have to think long and hard about even attempting it because he usually has 240 volts running through him.
Carlin:
Carlin is the kind of man who works with horses, which makes sense because his own nature is quite similar to these rather magnificent creatures. You see, horses are just like us humans in their capacity to express emotion, apart from one very important difference: horses never lie. 
You want to go and meet a genuine, considerate, humorous man? Go and meet Carlin. 
And I say humorous, although he doesn’t even realise it. If you asked him about his method of tick removal, for instance, he’ll advise you to pinch your fingers in hard at the base and rotate anti-clockwise, not clockwise. He’ll tell you why, that’s not for me to say. All you need remember is that truth and love are his only currency. Amen, Carlin.
Carlos: Carlos dances like his jocks are on fire and someone has just poured ice water over his burning nuts. So, he’s slow, and he’s cool, and he smiles, and he moves those hips and slides those shoulders like he’s really glad he still has the use of his Jonathan Livingston.
Carmen: An unusual name for a modern man, Carmen shrugs off the jibes about the female sound and heads off in the direction of relaxed life set-ups and successful experiments. He never gets flustered and as such makes a wonderful optimist. He too can be a kinky fucker.
Carmine: Old family money backs his endeavours and so Carmine tends to do okay. He’s a little gruff at times, which is only a wee defence mechanism he applies so’s not to appear vulnerable, but we suspect it’s because his dad was a bit serious, himself. Like all of us, the reactions of those who raise us arise from those who raised them, and at some point we all need to step out from beneath that umbrella and let the rain cleanse us to our true selves. Carmine will get there, and I trust you will too. Amen.
Carson: Carson will never succumb to the drudgeries of the poverty-stricken life, no sir. Good at negotiating deals out of the public eye, most of his skills in this realm are therefore only privy to a select few. Don't think he wont get his hands dirty if some actual hard work needs to be done, however. No, he's not used to getting mud and dirt on his hands, but if the group needs him to he'll mix it with the factory floor.
Carsten: The textbook science boffin with a giant, almost creepy smile. He’s very bright, always tucks his shirt in and never goes outside into the sun without a wide-brimmed hat. He makes very odd noises while making love, although, to be honest, we don’t want you to imagine that.
Carter: Carter is the name of an extremely shiny and well made box of condoms.
Cary: Cary will tell you that he loathes the spotlight. He's lying.
Cas: (Pronounced Cass) For a non-cussing man he does look quite serious, doesn’t he? We think it’s all a bit of a bluff, actually, although we’re not sure. His results here in his 5th season on tour are just splendid. We know he works hard behind the scenes and he has plenty of friends on the tour whom he competes against often, and while fiercely competitive out in the arena, on the sidelines afterwards he’s a picture of politeness. Perhaps that’s his secret to success?…that he keeps everything a secret.
Casey: Casey is perfectly contained and concentrated and while his decisions aren’t always well thought out, when he decides to act he moves like grease lightning. Regret = Bullshit.
Cash:
I'm not sure why his parents didn't call him Plenty of Cash, or perhaps, Yeah I've Got Twenty Bucks On Me, That'll Do Won't It?
As it is, Cash gets bored faster than a very fast thing running quickly on a fast moving train. He’ll need stimuli the whole time he’s here on Earth otherwise he’ll end up tearing things to pieces. He’d make a great lead singer of a rock band, but not one of these clean-living Christian bands that you hear about.
Caspar: The understated juggernaut who's never lost a game of hide and seek. Don't keep it all inside Caspar, is the advice from the universal gods. Let it out, and get out into the world. Search for opportunites and don't sit back waiting for them to come to you. It's a startling, beautiful place, this planet, and you belong out there lad!
Casper: You know how some vampires can transform themselves into a puff of smoke so they can get through doors and walls and such? Well, in that form they move like Casper and, to be honest, we up here in the commentary box don't really know how to describe his performance, other than to say his team doesn't often lose. You with me?
Cassidy: Is he dodgy? Well, no. Slippery sometimes, sure. Trustworthy, we think so. He's certainly a physically active individual. People often presume he's a bit rude, but only regarding how he won't talk to some people, although it only effects him in the work place. Occasionally we all need to deal with people we'd rather not deal with, but Cassidy does a good job of steering around that. Will it effect his prospects? Maybe, but that's only our perspective. Cassidy is his own cat, so I'd urge you not to worry about a thing.
Castellotti:
"Rejection? No not at all! That was her way of telling me that, while she's not ready for me now, she really wants me for later!"
The fact that white wine is dripping off his face here at the restaurant bar only tells him of how MUCH she wants that to happen.
That's Castellotti for you.
Cavey: Cavey loves attending masquerade balls because it fits into his life mantra of, whatever you do make sure you keep 'em guessing. He doesn't fulfill a regular job, some of his friends are even weirder than he is and he's broken several bones in several different climbing/trekking adventures.
Cayden: A skilled lacrosse player. Why? It's a fast game that requires speed and excellent hand-eye coordination, it's sometimes quite violent, although not maliciously so, which he enjoys, and it provides something of a routine in his life, which he needs. Cayden is a restless soul and we shudder to think what he'd get up to if he was left to roam the streets.
Cayson: Cayson is quite a useful informer. And he's smart enough to never do his deals in the public eye, unless he opts for the maximum public setting, like a football game or something.
Cecil: If he isn’t at least 75 years old, Cecil is weasely and limp-wristed.
Cedar: Well, I suppose we should be grateful they didn't call him Four Ply or Juniper Berry, eh? Anyway, Cedar is deep. At least, we hope he's deep. He might be just a little bit shy. Can't blame him of course. I’d be concerned too if my parents decided to name me something people make furniture from. But, he's a nice man. His heart beats slower than most and like many others in the Kingdom, his presence in a room has the effect of calming those around him. Rarely is Cedar out to get himself noticed.
Cedric: Cedric is a dairy farmer who speaks so quickly everyone assumes he’s telling one long undecipherable joke, which is both lucky and tragic because he’s bloody funny. Much to the lament of his wife, however, Cedric is absolutely useless in bed.
Ces: A doer. Better with men than with women and he’s never shied away from a hard day’s work. Big laugh. Overly strong handshake.
Cesar: Oh for fuck sake Cesar, you've done it again! (ie. With complete confidence he said he could fix the brakes on my car, but not two minutes out of the garage the brakes failed, but I was too caught up with the fire under the bonnet to notice. Now the fire brigade is coming. As my car burned I asked Cesar what he did and he apologised for forgetting about the brakes. Apparently he just had a little tinker with the carby' so it'd run better. Her only charged me $1200.) And look at him….he's still smiling. Unbelievable.
Chad: The boating, diving, fishing type. If he isn’t one of those, or he isn’t physically active in some significant way, then his ego takes over such that he becomes a grossly overconfident bore.
Chance: Chance is streamlined and highly skilled at whatever he does, and luck has very little to do with it.
Channing: Channing can sweet talk his way into and out of just about anything.
Chappy:
Man, this guy is quick. He barely sleeps. He's here, he's there. He's up trees and he's over dale. In the bar for ten minutes and he's already got itchy feet, but not before he nabbed the phone number of that cute brunette. Where's he off to now?.....The airport?.....NEW YORK??....What the hell for?.....(A conference on that pyramid scheme?)..... Are you for real?......

Moral to the story: Some people never switch off and so they can never sit still. Chappy.
Charles: The starfish that lives on the bottom of the ocean. He moves slower than anybody and he can regenerate a limb if it is eaten – it’s a slow process, after all. Charles may not be the first person you’d invite to the New Years Eve party at the Playboy Mansion but at least he doesn’t drink much.
Charley: The back end of his name catches you off guard, like a soft and subtle catcher's mitt in baseball, and he's nowhere near as reckless as he sounds. Maybe he's a Libran and maybe he ain't, but as a peaceful mediator he does his job very well. Rarely does have calluses on his hands.
Chas: Christ, what a unit. Even breathing is enough to get him excited.
Chase: Chase wanted to be an accountant until his teachers realised that he couldn't bloody count. These days he works with Darren, and he probably makes more money anyway. (Although he does party with Ryan a bit, and not many people can keep that up for too long, let me tell you.)
Chasen: The only thing Chasen is chasing is a fully open-minded approach. Don't get caught up around fences (or other peoples' whims) lad, get out there in the wind and discover your own belief system.
Chay: The rumours are true - Chay has been fired for insubordination before. It's official and so you can look it up in the records. What you won't read is that on each occasion Chay has been working for a boss who was a dangerous and beligerent idiot. Chay doesn't care about his official record and he'll talk about his experience freely. If you can find him, that is. He's quite the rover.
Chayce: Chayce gets a manicure every Friday lunchtime.
Chaz: The flamboyant Italian who made good. His daughters are gorgeous but woe-betide any man he catches looking at them for too long.
Chenar: Chenar takes chances, but not silly ones. He's quite a thoughtful and introspective fellow and he enjoys a healthy diet.
Chester:
Chester runs one of two ways: Either his parents are rich enough to send him to Harvard (law/economics), where his sense of entitlement runs his life, turning him into a painfully arrogant misogynist, or it’s a nickname given to a fellow with a perpetual smile on his face, a plethora of adoring friends in his midst (both male and female) and whose main aim in life is to avoid responsibility and have fun at all costs.
So, who you got?
Chevy: Well, it’s better than Hyundai, eh? Anyway, Chevy doesn’t blast his way through walls like his mother intended. He’s actually far more circumspect than that and he’ll often take his time when making a decision. As a hands-on man however, he likes to finish what he begins and he hates wearing a suit.
Chi:
People travel from all over the world to see him and endure many hardships on their once in a lifetime pilgrimage. They know that, if they can get to him, the knowledge gleaned from The Grand Master will be worth it.

In essence, what he will tell you is this: the answer lies within...
Chibiabos: Yeah, well, you'd love Chibiabos to be your boss because we all love a captain who really doesn't care if you turn up to work or not, although that's not strictly fair. Talk about juggling more than 5 balls at once and retaining a sense of humour! Chibiabos seems to carry this off. With a naturally low resting pulse, he rarely gets highly stressed and he probably needs to remember to exercise.
Chip: Chip is one of those guys people like to talk about. Is he gay? Is he a genius? Is he a psychopath? Is it true about what he did? …The rumours never end and as Oscar Wilde once said, the only thing worse than being talked about is not being talked about. We love Chip either way but, no, he’s not a macho fuckwit, no matter where in the field he chooses to play. Beyond all that rubbish, Chip is smarter than 93% of people in the room and he has a wonderful sense of humour. Amen.
Chito: If modern society ever regresses back into Roman times by allowing the major television networks to produce a game show whereby people win prizes by killing other people, then Chito will be a world champion at dispatching others with a spear from surprisingly large distances.
Chongo: Mr Disco at night. Plastic surgeon during the day. Like the Great Monkey (of Pigsy, Sandy and Tripitaka, fame) Chongo is world famous and irrepressible.
Chopper: Chopper needs no introduction. Look him in the eye, retain a sense of humour and always speak the truth (so long as your dealings in life are honourable). He might have been violent once but not any more…even so, obeying those aforementioned rules is a fine life plan anyway. Chopper himself is easy to pick in the wild because of his trademark moustache and beard formation.
Choppy: No use telling you his real name because even he has trouble spelling it, so Choppy it is. And what a specimen we have. Yes, sure, he moves reasonably quickly and easily, in the same way his mind deals with change and strangers, and as an ardent optimist he tends to adore both. Choppy has a certain kind of charisma which makes him eminently loveable and he can tell a funny and true tale in the most trying of circumstances. Not bad eh? The only flippant thing about Choppy is his name.
Chris: Chris is far more complicated than his female counterpart. As a mole that lives in the ground, he lives a neat, organised and dignified life that, on an outrageous day, could nearly be described as mysterious. Ensure that you don’t mess up the entrance to his burrow, however, because he’s liable to get quite angry.
Christian: Christian either reads too much of the Bible or snorts too much cocaine. Perhaps both.
Christoph: Yes, his ego might run at you like a North American grizzly bear, but he’s all bluff and bluster. Christoph drives an abnormal motor car, has an eclectic group of artistic friends who, like him, tend to be on the snobbish side and, like a few others out there in the Kingdom, he rarely get his hands dirty. Having said all that, however, he’s an incredibly intelligent and proud individual which results in memorable projects, so it’s not like he doesn’t ever leave a legacy.
Christopher: Teased by the boys at school for his lack of sporting prowess - and their jealousy of his academic success - Christopher got his own back when he took over daddy's multinational. And that's all wonderful, but no one knows that every Thursday night he sneaks a quick look over his shoulder before he steps through a dark doorway of a dingy little bar in the red light district that caters for just about anything. There had to be a reaction sometime.
Chuck: Chuck snaps his finger a lot, and he's constantly on the lookout for the next deal/girl/scam/cheap car.
Chum: Chum attacks life like a lion attacking a gazelle, except there’s never any harm or malice in his method because all he’s really trying to do is encourage the gazelle to rejoice in its life so much that it begins to radiate light. Personal motto: Have disco, will travel.
Ché: With a spirit that is stripped and pure to the core, Ché lives in the moment. He understands how good and bad deeds procure the future in very different ways, although he struggles to reconcile the notion that, here on Earth, at least, it seems nigh-on-impossible to have one without the other.
Cian: Cian doesn't pass a 10 cent coin in the street without picking it up. (Secretly he would like to pick up the 5c coins too but he's embarassed about what others might say.) Some advice: Cian, why give a rats rissole about what other people think? They don't really care what you do so long as it doesn't effect them.
Ciaran: Mmm...interesting. His decisions are never made public and no one knows who he is seeing. Extremely bright, he is, but his curiosity is largely kept away from the paparazzi. Ciaran knows what he wants and he doesn't give a flying rats arse about anything else, let alone what people make of his endeavours. He's travelled plenty and he remembers just about all of it. But dont think he's nasty. He's exactly the opposite.
Cid: You know how some people just have that warm, friendly fuzz about them? Awkward strangers feel happy and relaxed around them, the opposite sex gravitate towards them and a room full of weirdness and ill-feeling is immediately vanished with a collective sigh of relief when they enter the room. It might be his smile, his eyes, or it might be because he has saltwater in his veins, but Cid is a delicious chunk of love and fun, and we’re so glad he finally got here.
Cillian: No, Cillian doesn't dilly dally. Designed for peering around (and getting around) corners unseen and unheard, Cillian isn't one to waste either time or energy. Indeed, many might deem him to be a somewhat diffident lad. Maybe he is, but I doubt it. One suspects he's just saving his energy to spend it on people he respects because he definitely knows who he is. Old Cillian is no fool, and he cant be badgered into anything.
Cimarron: Is he a black man? He should be. He's a funky dude who, like Thiago way later, tends to look like he's dancing even when he's walking. Is he reliable? Should we employ him? Well, not if you want to move the company forward and increase your bottom line. It all depends on how happy you want your employees to be. They'll definitely be more productive with Cimarron around. Does that help?
Civa: (Pron. Sivva) There are some people you meet in life who you adore on sight. Civa is one of these cats. If he turned up at work in a superhero outfit you wouldn’t be surprised. If he donated a month’s salary to Medecins Sans Frontieres no one would bat an eyelid, not that you’d find out about it. If he flitted off to Hong Kong to sell some art, we’d take it in our stride and fill-in for him. And if he spent three days hold up in a hotel room with his betrothed covered in the juice of life, we’d only smile with the amount of fun they had. Such is Civa and such is life.
Clancy: The Fancy Dancy Doodley Dancy Man. Yes, he's a bit stupid but we love him, nonetheless.
Clarence: Clarence has a huge lung capacity and a very low resting pulse. He is therefore quiet and peace-loving 99.2% of the time. (Note: Just beware of the remaining 0.8%.)
Clark: A tall, thinking bin for recycling waste. He never moves quickly and while he is something of a control freak, he's rarely angered.
Clarky: Mr. Irreverant. Clarky will tell you that if you want to go and do something (eg. surfing, mud-crabbing, cafe building) then you should probably just go and do it.
Claude: Without doubt Claude is the laziest person on earth. He drags his feet when he walks and he lives for breakfast in bed.
Claudio: Claudio is one of the few people who, in the course of giving someone a genuine compliment, often gets his words mixed up such that the complimentee generally wants to argue/fight with him. It's quite a bizarre, if not funny feature of his life. (Claudio, we appreciate it. So keep up the good work!)
Clay: Maximally alert, he ain’t, but Clay is definitely solid. (Get him away from the city ASAP.)
Clayton: Peanut butter. (i.e: he’s liked by all, offensive to very few, he’s memorable for 3 minutes and all kids love him.)
Clem: The farmer with the old man’s soul. The climate is heating up, which isn’t going to make his life any easier, but he also knows that there’s no point being too glum about it either.
Cletus:
“Well hot dog, Cletus! I found me some biscuits just there on the ground. Want some?” 
Cletus looks around, looks at the biscuits, they look good. He reaches, because he knows a good thing when he sees one, and he’d never knock back free food, no matter where it came from.
Cleve: Some days you don't feel like being surprised by anything and Cleve is a fine example. We usually know where he is, we know what he's up to, we know who is hanging out with and we know where he works. And he's happy - we're definitely aware of that. If he was unhappy we're pretty sure we'd know about it although he has plenty of friends who would cheer him up. Cleve.
Cliff: Cliff has a wonderful, dry sense of humour and he was raised in a time when hard work and a kind word were important qualities in a person, and not just a throw away line in a social media feed.
Clifford: If he isn’t a wonderful traditional artist and he has no other nickname, then he is a boring white-fella who fulfils a sufficiently unexciting, middle-class house/life/philosophy. Ironic, eh? The former has barely spent a night under a roof and so is attached to the stars and the skies like you could not imagine…
Clint: Once he's out on the ground the boy can run, and there is no questioning his above-average intelligence and cunning but, yes, Clint, the word, is across between a clit and c_nt and while people down through the generations have deliberately mis-written his name on name tags, school bags, across the sky from the back of a plane and everywhere, basically, Clint is the man who has to wear it. Indeed, many Clints rise up and become great purely because of the fun pointed at them but, unfortunately, there is a high probability that Clint is nimble-minded douche bag.
Clinton: By default, Clinton is upright and diligent but this is only one facet of this rather unique organism. His name sounds like it has been poured into a mould of perfect conformity and efficient management, and it’s so formal, in fact, that he has actually passed out the other end of that spectrum to become one of the world’s great eccentrics.
Clive: Clive is so clumsy that, on average, he falls over three times every week. But, generally speaking, because he appreciates the world as being one of the funniest things he’s ever heard of, more often than not when he does fall over he’ll remain on the ground for some time afterwards laughing at his own self. It’s a beautiful thing.
Clyde: If the King ever needs to send a secret message that will avert war and save the Kingdom, then Clyde would be a prime candidate for the mission. Why? Because he's exactly not what the enemy spies would be expecting. He's cannier than the nearest fox and that time he takes leaving the house isn't because he's lazy, it's because he thinks things through. (And, yes, when it comes down to it, if he ever fell over and ruptured a lung it'd take him three days to feel the pain.) Amen young Clyde.
Clynt: (Man, that was close.) Clynt treats most situations in life as some kind of lottery prize and he is therefore rather gifted and enigmatic.
Clynton: The name of a Picasso painting that recently sold at auction for $112 million. How did that happen?? (And yes, Clynton is either an eccentric genius or a rather lovely, naive buffoon.)
Codi: Codi? OCD? Well, sort of, but then again, not really. He’s more like the manic-depressive without the depressive. Better than that, he’s not even that manic, but he does have mountainous reserves of energy. So, you better hope he has a dedicated ambition for something coz’ if this boy is left to run rampant he’ll terrorise the neighborhood in the same way a small, bored, psychotic Jack Russell tears apart your living room while you’re out. The flip-side is that once he’s focused, you won’t see a more inventive or driven young man. Indeed, these energy levels mean Codi will never properly ‘grow up’, and that is only a wonderful thing.
Cody: Affable and cosy to deal with, Cody is well positioned to use this empathy for his own ends, which he occasionally does, either deliberately or subconsciously. (Having said all that, he might be incredibly boring.)
Coen: Coen is a good competitor without being ruthless and never would he be hauled-up in front of an anti-corruption commission.
Cohan: Cohan presents a nice mix of indoors and outdoors. He's not prone to putting on weight and he is sufficiently adventurous.
Cohen: Cohen keeps a large chunk of his dreams and desires hidden away. He'd never get sprung like Jake, for instance, for Cohen is far more aware of his surroundings, not to mention the consequences of his actions.
Col: The tall and slightly out of shape middle-aged bouncer, who works at the pub every Sunday afternoon. He’ll kick people out if he has to, and he can handle himself, but overall all he wants to do is see that the young kiddies have a good time without hurting either themselves or anyone else. His home life is actually very sedate.
Colby: Colby has more secret compartments in his bedroom - and therefore his life - than anyone.
Colesy:
Fuckin' Colesy. So, he goes to Burma on a whim to get away from it and to see what's out there. Four weeks in, and he's in the middle of the jungle delirious with malaria, starving hungry because of all the opium he's smoked and in piss-poor health in general. Not far from broke but definitely close to death, he has a fevered, shivering dream, one night, of meeting an old man carrying bags of lychees. Next day, he's staggering down a beaten track next to banana trees too ripe to eat. He reaches for his water bottle. It's empty. This is it, he thinks. I'm screwed. Today's the day. Then, in front of him a tiny old man with no teeth emerges from out of nowhere, holding up two fists full of lychees, his big toothless grin lighting up the sky for hundreds of miles around.
This sort of shit happens to Colesy all the time.
Colin: Colin nearly disappeared during WWI because all of them were used as cannon-fodder by the British Army. As fate would have it, he now grows the best roses in the world. So, yes, many Colins are older, but regardless, those Colins who are deeply loving, and who inscribe warmth and compassion into every interaction, and not all of them do, are some of the world’s most beautiful people. True story. Never forget that a good Colin is an absolute gem.
Collins: A good panel-beater who actually thinks better when he’s underwater.
Colton: Colton hates being wrong and he definitely hates losing. Perhaps he needs to learn to laugh at himself a bit more? It’s hard to say.
Conan: So, his parents wanted Arnie for a son? Aside from that weirdness Conan is so sick and tired of that reference that he’s almost become shy. I say almost. He’s most assuredly a placid, peace-loving man. Perhaps he’ll find pure serenity away from all humans amidst the lushness of well-tended garden?
Concetto: No, he ain’t no icecream, he’s a self-employed man who works hard and who is very gullible. Even his kids can take the piss. He doesn’t mind.
Connar:
Jimmy or a Nick, Connar is considered, he is thoughtful, he is kind and he is fair, putting the needs of others first. Indeed, Connar, you would make a wonderful teacher who would make a mark on his students. I’d suggest grief counselling too, but you’re a sensitive man and that kind of job might get you down more than most. Suffice to say, if there were more Connars in existence the world would be a much calmer and safer place than what it is. 

(Note: Connar is totally unrelated to Connor/Conor in that he has never stolen anything, deliberately embarrassed anyone or behaved in a remotely immoral fashion...or so his mother assures us.)
Connor: Mate, if you insist on leaping into this river where you can see snags and submerged trees all about, do yourself a favour by at least jumping feet first, okay? (Yes, you're the same as Conor.)
Conolly: Connolly dances like a chicken that's accidentally pecked at a tab of acid rather than a some kind of seed. It's all a flail of arms and legs, which isn't dissimilar to how he functions in the office. Yes, he's an 'office' kind of guy.
Conor: Mate, if you insist on leaping into this river where you can see snags and submerged trees all about, do yourself a favour by at least jumping feet first, okay? (Yes, you're the same as Connor.)
Conrad: A powerful man who, as a means to show that he really isn’t infertile, loves nothing more than travelling to far-away lands and slaying as many natives as possible in the name of progress.
Coop: Doesn’t matter if he’s new to the area or new to the line-up, if there are waves to be had, Coop will bluster his way to middle of the take-off zone immediately and give shit to anyone who even looks like getting in his way.
Cooper: Cooper drives a late model BMW and spends a fortune on clothes and dry cleaning bills. He subscribes to the Financial Review and he ensures he leaves a copy in the front seat of his car but, aside from his these macho fantasies, he’s alright.
Coops: The Harley mechanic who, like any devoted artist, lives and breathes his passion. If he ever fell asleep across his chopper with his shirt off, you’d be hard pressed to discern the paintings on his body from the paintings on his bike.
Corby: Careful in life. Watchful with money.
Corey:
Quite the successful businessman, Corey will tolerate tyre-kickers for only so long. If a potential customer comes into his store for the third time, having bought nothing on the previous two visits, they can expect to be greeted with a sawn-off shotgun pointed at them.
“You must be eager to get something, sir? I’m glad you’re back. What would you like?” Corey will ask politely, his finger on the trigger.
The patron never leaves empty handed and everyone goes home happy.
Corie: Corie shies away from decisions that will count. Artistic, yes, but he needs to attend to this matter of life more than he is.
Cormac: Never sets foot outside the house with a blemish on his clothes. Sure, he might get dirty, he might end up brawling (as a younger man) and he might get blood and grease on him from helping a damsel in distress, and that's okay. But, present well at the start and the rest will follow - this is Cormac's main mantra.
Cornelis: Creative but unlucky, Cornelis has recently enlisted the help of an internet dating service and, on paper, he's doing well. He's had plenty of dates and they've been nice girls, but every time he's taken a girl to a restaurant for dinner she has managed to fall ill just as the desserts are brought out. It's never a ploy to leave early, and they like his company, it's just Cornelis's luck. Keep trying Cornelis, and we know he will because his enthusiasm is difficult to dampen.
Cornelius: The Glider. Unless he's the Cornelius who has just been plucked from the sea after the ship sunk and is still panicking despite the lifeboat being not that full and the ocean reasonably calm.
Corrado: Well what did you think was going to happen Corrado? If you ride a horse with no clothes on of course your nuts are going to get squashed. Come on dude, think about it…
Corrin: Corrin possesses more male beauty products than almost any other non-female in the Kingdom. Facial scrubs, cleansers, anti-wrinkle crap – you name it. He has the softest hands in the world.
Cors: Remember that scene in the movie Good Will Hunting when Matt Damon successfully defends himself in court, knowing full-well he’d broken the law? That’s Cors’.
Cortland: Cortland is that racehorse bought at the yearling sales as a creature that showed promise. He trained well and raced within his limits. He even won a few races in the country and in his only run in the big smoke he ran fourth. These days he's eating grass and hoping to meet a mare.
Cosie: Okay, if his name is pronounced as 'Cozzie' we suggest you head on over to Cozzie and it's all pretty good. If it's pronounced as 'Cosy', then he's a different breed of otter altogether. His schemes are more hidden, as are his friends, and he is far more territorial. Got all that?
Cosmo:
Is he a labourer?
No.
Is he an astronaut?
No.
Does he perfrom lewd acts for money?
...No.
Does he possess many friends?
Yes.
Is he human?
...Yes.
Can he cook?
Yes, but he's messy.
Can he speak different languages?
Sometimes.
Is he covered in paint like Jackson Pollock?

Bingo.
Costa: Yes, he does accost people, but only with love and humour and plenty of light. What more is there to say? Costa is a remarkable gem. The End.
Courtney: More feminine than his female counterpart, Courtney is about as useful as a tub of margarine that has been left outside near the barbecue overnight, and is now a partially melted lump with all manner of crumbs and meat clippings caked all over it.
Coxy: Coxy is a charismatic man who has a multitude of dodgy contacts, not to mention a sprinkle of even dodgier vices.
Cozzie: One of the leaders of the pack, Cozzie has mostly male friends and he's very quick on his feet.
Craig: A complex mathematical equation, the solution of which will assist us in understanding how the universe and human society as a whole are going to evolve. IBM’s Deep Blue supercomputer had a crack at it back in the day, but it suffered a meltdown and no one has been game to tackle it since. I wonder what the solution is?…
Crandall: Don't let the clean socks fool you. Crandall is a kinky fucker who knows how to have fun. And no one knows about it.
Crash: Difficult to ignore, Crash is an impressive individual who is anything but demure.
Crawf: Crawf’s reaction to hearing his name called anywhere is not dissimilar to a bubbly fox terrier’s whose owner stops, looks at them, pauses and then with a big smile says, “…..Walk?”
Crawford: MI6, The Federal Police, FBI, CIA, NSA, ASIO, etc etc etc. And he's kinky, although he'd kill you if you ever mentioned it in a public setting.
Creed: For such a smooth, single-shot sounding name Creed possesses a ferocity that only a scant few will ever get to witness or experience. He’s rarely the loudest person in the room and no, he’s not a brawler, although if he needed to fight his way out of a corner he’d very quickly take on the mantra of Kill Or Be Killed, and rightly so. Creed’s actions speak louder than words and he couldn’t give a rat’s arse about things like political systems and bureaucracy.
Crewe: Reliable and real, Crewe doesn't need to attach himself to a crowd as a means of survival and he only laughs at things that affect him deeply. Yes, it means some question his sense of humour, but these people need his attention more than he needs theirs.
Cris: Remember Liquid Paper? As something of clean-freak and an organised man, on and off the paper, to this day it remains the best invention Cris has ever seen. You can't say he never applies himself to a task, however.
Crispin:
Unusual name. Easy smile.
Organised, present, never wasteful: these are some of the impressions Crispin leaves in his wake. What you may not be aware of is that he is also rarely hyper-conservative, seldom dull or lifeless, and never pessimistic.
Crocket: Crocket has his hand on it, but he takes it as it comes and he does most things in his life pretty easily, as a result.
Crofto: Crofto has woken up on a beach in front of a dying campfire, surrounded by passed-out bodies and warm cans of half-drunk beer, more than nearly anyone.
Cruz: The crew up here in the commentary box are pretty sure Cruz is intended to rhyme with booze and not buzz. Be that as it may, is Cruz out of bed yet? And how can we conduct an interview with a man who doesn't own shoes, Cruz? It's a good question...
Cuan: Careful to see that procedures are followed through to their natural end, Cuan rarely jumps into situations impulsively. It's just how it is. He'd be good at working for a team that is trying to maximise the aerodynamics of either a race car or an aircraft.
Curly: As an aboriginal in a past life and a gifted artist in this one, he is a seeker of truth whose passions live on his sleeve. Make of that what you will, but love drips out of his pores like the sweat of a beautiful black man that has just walked into the Derby pub, having left Broome about three days ago in the middle of the wet. (Note: If asked about the state of his phallus, he will reply that he is in possession of an “evil cock”.)
Curt: He’s never said a prayer for anything he’s ever killed in his life, regardless if it was an antelope he shot with a rifle, a bug he squashed with his foot or a kangaroo he hit with his car. Yeah, Curt is a real softie…(just kidding!). We struggle to envisage how he manages his romantic life in a fun and gentle manner, but there must be outliers of the Curt species who are just lovely, right?….Anyone met one?
Curtis: Curtis possesses a highly acute acumen and he promises much.
Cuthbert: He’s never picked a fight in his life - well, aside from one time at university when the reputation of a lady friend was questioned - and his work life operates at a managerial level, which makes sense. He sports an ego and he enjoys succeeding at tasks which require deep analysis and lots of preparation.
Cy: Cy doesn't just solve problems, he pulverizes them.
Cybil: Mmm, Cybil likes a clean establishment. He loves watching the Tour de France, whether drugs are involved or not, and he likes the aerodynamic nature of the outfits they wear. Beyond that, who knows!
Cyril: Cyril lives alone with his dog up in the hills, he brews his own liquor and he shoots rabbits that they both share. Sometimes he cooks them, sometimes he doesn’t.
Cyrus: Extremely calculating, Cyrus is in the secret service. His Directors prefer to remain ignorant of how he manages to extract the amount of information he does from his 'sources'.
